correctness.rationale: The specified Herschel graph is exactly the 18-edge, 11-vertex object in RESULT.md. BFS and Floyd-Warshall agree on all pair distances. Every nonempty subset is examined for r=0,...,4; r=2 has 178 faces and 526 Hasse covers. The explicit ordered vertex-toggle matching has 88 distinct face pairs and only one zero-face and one three-face critical. Exhaustive directed-cover topological sorting proves acyclicity, yielding \(S^3\) by integral discrete-Morse theory (one 0-cell and one 3-cell). At r=3 all 767 elementary pairs are individually checked as free and maximal, leaving vertex zero. r=1 is the connected triangle-free 11-vertex 18-edge graph with cycle rank eight, and r=4 is the full simplex. Exactly 12 graph automorphisms are forced by degrees, realized by S3 x C2, and their oriented face-chain Lefschetz traces give the stated product sign degree on integral top homology. These disjoint-stage homology supports determine the barcode over every field. The complete checker and its output are included; mod-two homology is corroboration rather than replacement for the integral homotopy proof.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the canonical smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph; the exact shortest-path Rips filtration is a natural invariant of that named object rather than an arbitrary slice. Its scale-two flag complex has 5-dimensional simplices yet the integral homotopy type \(S^3\), followed by an explicit scale-three simplicial collapse. This identifies a meaningful topology jump; all-field persistence and the nontrivial S3 x C2 integral orientation character refine Betti data and yield a rationally acyclic quotient. The finite, small-instance scope is openly stated and no broad graph-family theorem is inferred.
